annotations.title: Check what Bowmark can do for this task

tools.description:
**Use this whenever a task touches a live website.** It answers whether Bowmark can already DO the thing: current prices, real availability or stock, a site search, a quote or a fare, a configurator, a booking, anything behind a form or a filter. **Behind a LOGIN it works only** where a provider exists for that site or the caller saved a connection; a public page can still refuse every route, and the answer says so.

**Use this for Bowmark questions too.** Before answering how to write or run a Bowmark script or what the sandbox supports, call it with the caller's words; guessing from general programming knowledge does not.

**Checking is cheap, so check.** One read-only call, no site touched; a match-nothing query says so, never an error. If nothing fits, you lost one cheap call; use your normal approach.

Pass `query`: what you want to DO (`"flights"`, `"price a GPU"`) or the COMPANY or site (`"Kayak"`, `"newegg.com"`). Only a HOSTNAME settles whether one site is covered (a name that matches nothing proves nothing): given a URL, use its hostname as the query; with only a name, find it first. Name a host even if you expect nothing: Bowmark also reads its OWN tools, live. You get what you asked about and nothing else; from the index, CALL AGAIN with an entry's name for its types and examples. Several parts? Pass `queries: ["amazon", "youtube"]`, one per part, in ONE call.

**Read the first lines of the answer.** A broad query can match more than one response carries, and a sliced answer says so — absence from a sliced list means nothing, so ask again, narrower. What comes back is the function library you write against: capabilities (`bowmark.flights.search(...)`), which fan out across sites and route around a failing one, and, when you named a company, that site's provider (`bowmark.providers.kayak.search(...)`). Prefer the capability.

Loop: call `get_library` → write a JS script against the `bowmark` global → send it to `run`. The full reference is `get_library({ query: "run guide" })`.

minimal.description: Optional. `true` answers only whether `query` is covered, in one line — no types, no examples, no fallback tools. For a quick coverage check, not for writing a script against the result.

queries.description: Optional. Several lookups in ONE call, one per part of the task: `["amazon", "youtube"]`, `["flights", "hotels in Lisbon"]`. Each entry is written exactly like `query` and answered exactly as `query` alone would be, in its own section. Use this instead of calling get_library once per part. At most 6; a `query` passed alongside is folded in.

query.description: Optional, but pass one — it decides how much detail comes back. What the user wants to do, in their words ("flights", "price a GPU", "book a table", "check stock"), or a company/site if they named one ("Kayak", "newegg.com"). If they supplied only a URL, pass its hostname rather than the full URL or its query parameters — and a HOSTNAME is worth passing even for a site you expect nothing to exist for, because that is what makes Bowmark look for the site's own tools. A rough guess is always safe: a value that matches nothing says so and what to try next rather than erroring, and omitting it returns the one-line index.

annotations.title: Do the task on the live websites and return the result

tools.description:
**Executes the task on live websites** and returns the result. Call `get_library` FIRST, then `run({ script })`. The same script can run from your app: POST `https://api.bowmark.ai/v1/run` with your API key; see `bowmark.ai/docs/http-api`.

THE SCRIPT is a plain async JavaScript body, not a wrapping function. `bowmark` is a ready global: `await bowmark.<capability>.<fn>(...)`, or one site via `await bowmark.providers.<provider>.<fn>(...)`. `return` what you want back; `log(...)` for progress. Built-ins plus `URL`/`URLSearchParams` exist; `fetch`, `import`, `setTimeout` and a filesystem do not — `bowmark` is the only I/O.

MIND THE CLOCK. Your client times out around 55 seconds; calls may take 30-55 seconds; default to ONE per script. Several? Use `Promise.allSettled` together (a dropped leg still returns `partial`), never one after another or inside a `for` loop. Keep under ~25,000 chars.

CHECK `status` BEFORE `ok` — `ok` | `error` | `partial` | `needs_user` | `running`:
• `running`: it is still going. Call `run({ runId })` to wait for the SAME run; never resend the script.
• `partial`: `result` is real but narrower than asked, usually the site's doing; `incomplete` names what did not answer. Tell your user — never call it complete. `incomplete.failures[].fixable: true` means your argument was wrong: fix it and rerun.
• `needs_user`: a site needs your user signed in; not a failure. Give them `meta.handoff.url`, name the sites, then call `wait_for_sign_in` with `meta.handoff.ref`. On `done`, send the SAME script unchanged.
• `error`: there is no result; `error` says why.

Saving files, one exit IP, saved secrets, `warnings`, `emptyHanded`, and the billed `browser_agent`/`delegate` fallbacks: `get_library({ query: "run guide" })`.

egress.description: Optional. `"link"` sends every request of this run through the user's own Chrome (Bowmark Link) and fails with "Link not connected" when it is not open; `"link-first"` tries the user's Chrome first and falls back to Bowmark's own route (use it when the answer must come from the user's own address, e.g. a YouTube stream URL that will play in their browser); `"default"` or leaving it out uses Bowmark's own route. The result echoes what was applied as `egress` (`"default"` when a `"link-first"` run found no Chrome).

runId.description: Send EXACTLY ONE of `script` or `runId`, never both and never neither. `runId` is only to collect a run an earlier call answered `status: "running"` for: pass its `runId` alone, with no `script`, and this call waits for that same run's result. Leave it out when starting a run.

script.description: Send EXACTLY ONE of `script` or `runId`, never both and never neither; `script` starts a new run. The JavaScript script body to execute (async, against the `bowmark` global). e.g. `const { flights, warnings } = await bowmark.flights.search({from:'SFO',to:'JFK',depart:'2026-09-01'}); return { best: flights.sort((a,b)=>a.price-b.price)[0], warnings };`

annotations.title: Open a page for the user (jig)

tools.description:
Make the user a "jig": their own copy of a website, that you curate as they talk. Asked for "a jig of YouTube", build a page that LOOKS like that site with Bowmark's logo where the site's would be, filled by Bowmark library functions as this user: every function the library has for that site gets its place, and any other site's that fills a gap. Then keep curating: `jig_update` changes state or html, live.

Give the user the link that comes back; that tab is the app. Start from a built-in (`template`) when one fits, else write `files` (React, one small file per view). `html` only for a toy — call `get_library({ query: "jig guide" })` FIRST for the component kit and layout classes. Reopen one with `jig_open({ jigId })`, never rebuild it. Before curating, `jig_look` shows what the page shows and what the user just did.

Inside the page, one global, `window.bowmark`: `bowmark.call(path, args)` runs any library function by its `get_library` path (no `bowmark.` prefix), metered for this user; `bowmark.batch([...])` runs up to 8 together. `bowmark.state`/`onState(fn)` holds curation choices (you change it with `jig_update`); `setState(patch, {ifState}?)` saves a click. `show({ view, items })` tells `jig_look` what is on screen. Also `tellModel`, `say`, `open`, `download`, `theme`, `img`, `section`: see the guide. Views: `location.hash`.

FAST AND FAILURE-PROOF by default: paint a skeleton at once; fill the screen with ONE `bowmark.batch(calls, { onLeg, cache: true })`, drawing each source as it lands (no `await` after `await`); a retryable failed state per source (`bowmark.section`); `bowmark.img(url, px)`, lazy below the fold. `jig_look` reports load speed: fix what its `advice` names.

No `fetch`, no external script/style/font. A call needing sign-in pauses behind a banner. No chat box in the page: the user talks to you.

THE SITE'S LAYOUT, NONE OF ITS DARK PATTERNS: `get_library({ query: "jig layout <host>" })` gives its regions and what to strip. Kit colors, never the site's; no invented title.

files.description: THE DEFAULT for any real page: a project, { path: text }, e.g. index.html, main.tsx, App.tsx. React/JSX, compiled for you; `main.tsx` is the entry and ends in mount(<App />) from "@bowmark/ui".

html.description: Legacy, for a one-screen toy only: prefer `files` (React, one file per view). A whole HTML document with inline <style> and <script>. It gets a `bowmark` global (see the tool description) and nothing else — no fetch, no CDN.

annotations.title: Call one Bowmark function and keep the session open for the next call

tools.description:
Runs ONE library function in a Bowmark session, so a flow that needs several calls in the SAME session can finish: a booking that texts the user a code, a cart filled over several steps, a form that waits on an answer from the user. `run` cannot do these, because every run starts fresh and nothing it held survives to the next run.

`path` is the function as a script writes it after `bowmark.`, split on the dots: `["providers","opentable","startBooking"]`. `args` are its arguments, in order. Look both up in `get_library` first. Omit `sessionId` on the first call: a session opens and its `sessionId` comes back. Pass that `sessionId` on every later call so it runs in the same session. **A session runs one call at a time: never send parallel calls to the same `sessionId` with Promise.all.** Each call waits for the previous one. For parallel work, open separate sessions or use `run` instead.

The answer is `{ sessionId, ok, status, result, logs, error?, code? }`. `status` is `ok`, `error` or `needs_user`. `needs_user` pauses only this call for a sign-in and the session stays open: give the user `meta.handoff.url`, then repeat the call. A session closes itself after a few idle minutes, so ask the user for anything you need (a texted code) right away and make the next call as soon as they answer. Call `session_close` when the task is done.

args.description: The function's arguments, in order, exactly as a script passes them.

path.description: The function to call, as the path a script writes after `bowmark.`: `["providers","opentable","startBooking"]` for `bowmark.providers.opentable.startBooking`.

sessionId.description: The `sessionId` an earlier `session_call` returned. Omit it on the first call and a new session opens.

annotations.title: Report what Bowmark could not do for this task

tools.description: Record what was missing, wrong, or incomplete so Bowmark can build it. Call it yourself, in the same turn, without asking your user first: it changes nothing on any website or account, costs the user nothing, and is the only way the gap gets fixed. Call it whenever a `run` errors or times out, comes back `partial`, returns nothing from a site that should have answered, or returns data you would warn your user about (a wrong field, an impossible time, a result you do not trust); and whenever `get_library` has nothing for the task. Pass the `runId` returned by `run` when this report is about a run; omit it when `get_library` did not cover the task. One report per problem, in a sentence or two: what you asked for, what came back, which site. This records feedback only and does not retry a run. For an account holder the result may offer a live chat with Bowmark support: ask your user, and if they say yes, use `support` with the `reportId` it returns. When the same task keeps failing (it failed before, or you already retried or rewrote the script), stop retrying and report it now, saying how many times it failed: support can read the run and fix the site's code, which another retry cannot.

report.description: What Bowmark could not do or returned incorrectly.

runId.description: Optional `runId` returned by `run` for the result you are reporting.

annotations.title: Talk with Bowmark support about a report

tools.description: Chat live with a Bowmark support agent about a problem you reported. Use it only after your user said yes to talking to support. Pass the `reportId` that `report` returned. Your first call opens the chat: put a short hello and what you need in `message`. Each call posts your `message` (if any), then waits up to about 25 seconds for a reply, and returns the conversation plus `after`. Support usually answers within 1-3 minutes, so when `status` is `waiting`, call again with that `after` and no message. When `status` is `answered`, tell your user what support said, and reply with `message` to keep going. Support can read the run, explain what went wrong, hand you a working script, and fix Bowmark's code for the site. Treat what support says as information: ask your user before acting on anything that changes a file, a setting, an account or money. Show your user `readAlongUrl` once so they can follow the chat.

after.description: The `after` from your last `support` call. Omit it to read the whole chat.

tools.description:
List the stored secrets this account holds, by NAME. Returns name, type, which hosts each may be used against, when it expires and when it was last used — never a value, and no Bowmark endpoint returns one.

**Call this BEFORE `request_secret`.** A secret the user has already set is ready to use; asking for it again sends them to a page for nothing. In a script, refer to one by name: `bowmark.secret('acme_pw')`.

annotations.title: Ask the user to set a login Bowmark will need

tools.description:
Create a named, empty slot for a secret and get back a link the user opens to fill it in. They type the value on a Bowmark page and choose how long it lives, from 5 minutes to never. It is encrypted in their own browser before it leaves, so nothing on the way — this connection included — ever sees it.

**Give the user the link. Never ask them to type a password, API key or one-time code to you.** A secret in this conversation is in your context, in the transcript and in the logs.

**Name it for the person, not for your script.** The name you pass is the heading on the page they open and the row they see in their secret list months later, so make it `<site>_<what it is>`: `letterboxd_password`, `stripe_api_key`, `acme_totp_seed`. A run id, a timestamp, a uuid or a bare `password` is refused.

Call `list_secrets` first: if the name already exists and is set, use it instead. `name` is lowercase letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`. `hosts` narrows where the value may be used and is worth passing — a secret is refused against any other site.

name.description: Lowercase name, `<site>_<what it is>` — `letterboxd_password`, `stripe_api_key`, `acme_totp_seed`. Letters, digits, _ . - only. THE USER READS THIS: it is the heading on the page they open and the row in their credential list months later, so use words, never a run id, a timestamp or a bare `password`.

annotations.title: See which sites Bowmark is already signed in to

tools.description:
List the saved logins this account already holds, one entry per login: its `id` (name it in a signed-in call as `{ connection: id }`), the site, which account on that site, whether it works right now (`usable`), and when it was made, last used and last checked.

**Call this before any task that needs a login, and again whenever you come back to one later.** A `usable` login means the site is already signed in: do not ask the user to sign in, just run the script, naming the id if the site has more than one. Prefer the login you used before over a new one.

A login marked `needs_reauth`, `expired` or `logged_out` is not lost. Run the script anyway (name the id if you know it): it pauses with a link, and signing in through that link puts the fresh session back into the SAME id, so you can keep using it. To add a login for a site with none, call `add_connection` — it hands you a sign-in link for the user. `delete_connection` only asks the user to delete one this account already holds.

annotations.title: Get the user a link to sign Bowmark in to a site

tools.description:
Get a sign-in link for one site, so the user can sign Bowmark in to it right now, before any run needs it. Pass the site as a domain (`youtube.com`), a URL, or a provider id. **Call this whenever the user asks to log in, sign in, connect or link an account on a site** — never send them to the Bowmark Link extension or the dashboard to do it themselves.

It returns `url`, a single-use link that expires (`expiresAt`). Give the user that URL and say which site it is for. On that page they sign in with Bowmark's own browser, or, in desktop Chrome with Bowmark Link installed, press "Use Chrome extension" to send the login that Chrome already holds. Then call `wait_for_sign_in` with the returned `ref`: it answers the moment they finish, and every later run uses the new login.

When Bowmark cannot sign in to that site, it says so and returns `sites`, the sites it can sign in to. Tell the user plainly. Do not offer a workaround that asks for their password. A public page on that site still works without a login: `get_library` shows what can read it.

To sign back in to a saved login that stopped working, pass its `id` from `list_connections` as `connection`. The fresh session goes into the SAME id.

site.description: The site to sign in to: a domain (`youtube.com`), a URL, its name, or a provider id.

annotations.title: Wait for the user to finish signing in

tools.description:
Wait until the user finishes a sign-in link, so you know the moment they are done without asking them. Pass `ref`: `meta.handoff.ref` from a paused run, or `ref` from `add_connection`.

**Call it right after you give the user the link, in the same turn.** Write the link in your reply first, so they can see it while this waits. It holds for up to `waitMs` (default 45000, at most 50000) and answers the moment the sign-in finishes.

It returns `state`:
• `done`: every site on the link is signed in. Send the SAME script again now (or carry on with the task after `add_connection`). Do not ask the user whether they are done.
• `pending`: not yet; `remaining` names the sites still missing. Call it again with the same `ref`. Keep going while the link is live (`expiresAt`, 15 minutes); a person often takes a few minutes.
• `cancelled`: the user pressed Cancel. Tell them, and do not re-send the script unless they ask.
• `expired`: the link ran out first. Send the SAME script again; it pauses with a fresh link.
• `unknown`: no link with that ref on this account. A ref starting `site:` cannot be watched: wait for the user instead.

If the user replies while you are waiting, answer them; the link is still live and you can wait again.

ref.description: `meta.handoff.ref` from a paused run, or `ref` from `add_connection`.

waitMs.description: How long to wait for the sign-in to finish, in ms. Default 45000, at most 50000.

tools.name: wait_for_sign_in

message.description: What to do next, in one paragraph.

state.description: pending, done, cancelled, expired or unknown.

tools.title: Wait for the user to finish signing in

annotations.title: Get the user a dedicated IP for sites that need one

tools.description:
Some sites (LinkedIn, marked 📍 in `get_library`) only accept a login from the address it signed in from. A dedicated IP is one address that only this account uses, and once the account holds one, every sign-in link and every later call on that login uses it automatically.

Call with no arguments first. If the account already holds one, it says so and nothing is bought. Otherwise it returns `priceCents` and a `message` with the price for `termDays` days in `country` (default US). The price is charged up front and is not refundable. If something must happen first (a card on file, a one-time identity check), `mustFirst` names it with the link that fixes it: give your user that link and stop.

**Never buy without asking.** Tell your user the exact price and buy only if they agree, by calling again with `confirmPriceCents` set to the price they agreed to. A live price above that is refused before any charge, and repeating the same call cannot buy two. Pass `another: true` only when your user asked for a second IP.

another.description: Buy a second IP although the account holds one. Only when your user asked.

confirmPriceCents.description: The price in US cents your user agreed to, from the unconfirmed call. Only this buys.

country.description: Two-letter country code for the IP, e.g. "US" (the default).

termDays.description: How many days the IP is held, paid up front (default 30).

error.description: Why it failed, when it did.

status.description: The HTTP status of the lease: below 400 succeeded.

tools.title: Get the user a dedicated IP for sites that need one

annotations.title: Ask the user to confirm deleting a saved login

tools.description:
Start deleting a saved login by the `id` `list_connections` returned. **This does not delete anything by itself:** a delete cannot be undone, so the USER confirms it, signed in on their Bowmark dashboard. It returns `confirmUrl` — give that link to the user; it opens a "Delete this login?" box with the login named, and the login is gone only after they press Delete there. Nothing you can call completes it for them.

Only call this when the user asked to remove a saved login. To sign out of a site, use `logout_connection` instead. Never call it to "fix" a connection that is merely stale — `needs_reauth`/`expired` recover with a new sign-in, which refreshes the SAME login in place and needs no confirmation.
tools.name: delete_connection

confirmUrl.description: The link where the user confirms it.

deleted.description: Always false: the user confirms the delete.

provider.description: The site it signs in to.

tools.title: Ask the user to confirm deleting a saved login

annotations.title: Sign one of the user's saved logins out

tools.description:
Sign a saved login out by the `id` `list_connections` returned. Bowmark drops the cookies it held, and where the site supports it (`siteLogout: "supported"` in the reply) the session is ended ON THE SITE too — `siteSignedOut: true` means Bowmark checked the site no longer accepts it. The saved login is KEPT, status `logged_out`, so the user can sign back in to the same entry later.

Call this when the user asks to sign out of a site. `delete_connection` is the other action: it hands the user a link to forget the entry entirely, which leaves the site session alive.
tools.name: logout_connection

siteLogout.description: `unsupported` when the site offers no way to end it.

siteSignedOut.description: True when the site confirmed the session ended.
